rows.note: This is the all-purpose choice in formal or written contexts for moderating or softening something.

example.english: The government should temper the tension between the two sides.
example.traditional: 政府應該緩和雙方之間嘅緊張關係。
example.jyutping: zing3 fu2 jing1 goi1 wun4 wo4 soeng1 fong1 zi1 gaan1 ge3 gan2 zoeng1 gwaan1 hai6

rows.note: This is the all-purpose noun for a person's tendency to become angry or their general temper.

example.english: Their temper is awful; they snap at people over the smallest things.
example.traditional: 佢脾氣好臭，一少少事就鬧人。
example.jyutping: keoi5 pei4 hei3 hou2 cau3 jat1 siu2 siu2 si6 zau6 naau6 jan4

rows.note: Use this for someone's current mood or state of mind, whether good or bad.

example.english: My temper is a bit off today, so I don't want to go out.
example.traditional: 我今日心情麻麻，唔想出街。
example.jyutping: ngo5 gam1 jat6 sam1 cing4 maa4 maa4 m4 soeng2 ceot1 gaai1

rows.note: Use this for the anger or irritability behind an angry outburst, especially in casual speech.

example.english: Cool your temper first; don't yell so loudly.
example.traditional: 你收吓火氣先，唔好咁大聲鬧人。
example.jyutping: nei5 sau1 haa5 fo2 hei3 sin1 m4 hou2 gam3 daai6 seng1 naau6 jan4

rows.note: Use this for composure or self-control, especially the ability to remain steady under provocation.

example.english: You keep your temper even when people yell at you; that's impressive.
example.traditional: 你畀人鬧都咁有定力，真係難得。
example.jyutping: nei5 bei2 jan4 naau6 dou1 gam3 jau5 ding6 lik6 zan1 hai6 naan4 dak1
